The game is now out on Android on Google Play!

I posted my game, Unlimited Golf, earlier in the Sub. Since then a lot has changed and not much else has been posted in the sub. I have bug fixed, upgraded to Unity5, changed the physics, added tutorials, global highscores, and more.

You can now play the game on Kongregate! Click and check it out!

Rate the game and let me know what you think. Just because it is released doesn't mean things wont keep changing!

Some comments:

  • I thought it was pretty cool. I liked the Unity engine, although it loaded kind of slow.

  • The physics were almost annoyingly inconsistent. But I think that's because there's no way to tell how far back you drew your mouse for previous shots. It's hard to build an intuition on how to shoot shots. I found myself overshooting, then way overcompensating later. Maybe make a way to indicate how far back you've drawn the mouse? I don't know how much of the gameplay you're going to change.

  • How do I tell what kind of spin the ball has? I just kind of wondered that.

  • I like just cannoning the ball into the heavens just to see if I can moonshot the hole :P

The second point about shooting the ball I definitely think is a concern, but keep up the work! I should add I have no experience developing games, so this is all coming from a non-technical place.

I can tell you the physics are pretty damn consistent. What could be affecting it is, as you said, how far you are dragging and maybe wind. I've considered and am still playing with the idea of displaying shot power. However I think providing that information will make the game easier, something I don't want to do. I think with time you begin to just know how far back you need to pull for a good shot.

The ball never really has spin.

Shooting the ball up super high is always fun. I might make the sky fade to stars for extremely high shots. There is a special award if you can get the ball in from a shot like that too.

Also, I'm willing to change a lot about the game as it isn't out yet for mobile. I want to really perfect the game and keep putting in work. Thanks for the feedback!

Following this news on TV right now.

Conflicting initial reports, once again in after-earthquake news in the Indian sub-continent.

I've found through different sources that it was 7.4, and near Kodari, Nepal. Also, the Richter scale was designed in the 30's and more so for west coast US earthquakes. The new scale is called the Moment Magnitude Scale, (M or MMS) and it's been that way since the 70's. (Even if the news says Richter scale it is likely MMS, and the only reason is that is more badass to say on air).
